raw_response:
Answer: A
Reason: Following a pneumothorax and subsequent lung reexpansion, the azygos fissure often becomes more prominent on chest X-ray (Figure 3a) compared to baseline (Figure 1a) due to pleural thickening or separation within the fissure. The teardrop-shaped opacity (azygos vein) typically remains visible, ruling out options suggesting its absence or unchanged appearance.
